analysis.body:
Per the Census Bureau, 36.5% of finance and insurance firms, NAICS 52, reported using AI in the last two weeks, compared with 40.0% in the prior period. The survey first asked this question in September 2023. This figure covers the broad finance and insurance sector rather than banking alone.

Per Evident Insights, the Evident AI Index benchmarks AI adoption across financial services and scores major global banks on talent, innovation, leadership, and transparency. Evident describes several of the world's biggest banks as having quietly become AI-powered behemoths and says banks are racing to incorporate the technology into almost everything they do. The page's own summary notes that fraud detection and credit models are decades old, while generative AI in service and compliance is the new frontier.

Per The World of AI, the site tracks the 1,000 most-downloaded open financial models on the Hugging Face Hub, with licence, downloads, and release date refreshed daily, including models tuned for financial text. This indicates a supply of open models, but the excerpts do not report vendor concentration or spending figures.

Per the Federal Reserve, credit and AML models operate under SR 11-7 model risk management guidance issued in 2011, meaning banking AI governance predates the current AI boom by more than a decade. Per Treasury, its report on AI in financial services, covering uses, opportunities, and risks, frames the US supervisory conversation. The Treasury excerpt in the source material concerns sanctions enforcement rather than AI specifics, so no detailed risk findings are available here.

The excerpts do not report ROI evidence or dollar figures. A reader deciding whether to deploy should note that banking already has mature model risk rules, that adoption in finance and insurance is measurable but the latest Census reading is lower than the prior period, and that open financial models are catalogued and refreshed daily. The material does not provide enough vendor or return data to support a specific purchase decision.

https://evidentinsights.com/.brief: Evident Insights is an intelligence platform that benchmarks and tracks AI adoption across the financial services sector. It supplies data, research, and benchmarking to help financial services leaders make informed AI-related decisions, investments, and strategic choices. The platform publishes the Evident AI Index, which ranks banks and insurers on their AI deployment and highlights emerging trends. Since launching in January 2023, the index has sparked debate and received widespread press coverage, with Evident CEO Alexandra Mousavizadeh frequently commenting on global AI trends.

https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-rel.brief: On International Anti-Corruption Day, Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control sanctioned 28 individuals and businesses tied to a Zimbabwe-based gold smuggling and money-laundering network led by Kamlesh Pattni. The Treasury says the scheme bribed officials, used trusted supporters to conceal ownership, and built a global web of companies to hide illicit activity, depriving Zimbabwe’s citizens of resource benefits while enriching corrupt officials and criminals. Acting Under Secretary Bradley T. Smith noted that “Corruption respects no borders” and that the action demonstrates a whole-of-government approach and collaboration with allies. The Treasury’s move is carried out under Executive Order 13818, which targets serious human-rights abuse and corruption worldwide. International Anti-Corruption Day, observed annually on December 9 since the 2003 UNCAC, aims to raise awareness of anti-corruption initiatives; the United Nations lists 189 parties to the convention.

https://www.federalreserve.gov/supervisi.brief: This page lists the Federal Reserve Board of Governors’ 2011 supervision and regulation letters. It notes that a lock icon or https indicates a secure .gov connection and advises “Share sensitive information only on official, secure websites.” It also contains guidance on prior notices concerning dividend declarations by savings association subsidiaries of savings and loan holding companies.

https://theworldofai.org/ai-ecosystem/te.brief: The World of AI reports that this page catalogues the 1,000 most-downloaded open financial models on the Hugging Face Hub. Each entry includes its licence, download count, and release date, and the list is refreshed daily. The data comes from the Hugging Face Hub public API, sorted by all-time downloads, and every model links to its own Hub page. The page was last verified on 22 September 2026.
